Maya, a woman in her late twenties, South Asian, olive skin, no makeup, faint under-eye shadows, dark wavy hair in a messy bun with loose wisps. Same in every shot: oversized cobalt-blue crewneck sweatshirt, charcoal leggings, white sneakers, plain dark smartwatch on her left wrist with a matte black unlit face. Her hands are empty.
Street: SoHo cobblestones, red brick buildings, blank unlettered awnings, plain closed shutters, wet asphalt, flat overcast daylight, neutral white balance.
Look: wide-normal lens, camera fixed on sticks, no camera movement, one continuous shot, documentary realism, visible skin texture, fine grain. Muted grey and brick, Maya the only saturated colour. Heads in the middle third, top and bottom of frame kept clear.
Rules: no text, letters, numerals, signage, logos or lit screens anywhere in frame. Maya does not talk to anyone. Exactly five strangers, and nobody enters or leaves frame except Maya.
Maya is centre frame in a medium-wide, walking slowly toward camera down the middle of the street, five strangers crowded tight around her, leaning at her face, mouths moving, all talking at once. The full crowd is there from the very first frame, no build-up.
audio: dense unintelligible street murmur, many overlapping voices, traffic, footsteps, no music, never silent.
The three nearest her: a man in his thirties in green flannel, waving both palms forward urging her on; a woman in her forties in a brown blazer, cutting across him, one flat palm raised telling her to stop; an older man with a grey beard, shrugging, both hands turned up. Nobody is hostile, all genuinely trying to help, contradicting each other in gesture as much as in words. They look at Maya, never at the lens. The five shift and step around her, closing the gap.
Finally Maya slows and stops in the same medium-wide, all five still around her and still talking. Eyes open, jaw set, looking straight ahead past the lens. Her left arm hangs at her side, wrist and watch unobstructed, nobody in front of it. Hold to the last frame.
